doc.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003

title: Teen band with Freddie Hubbard and James Spaulding; first road gig
summary: Their teenage band played six nights a week at a club, with Al Plank on piano; he took a first road gig at sixteen with the Jazz Contemporaries.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: It’s okay. You’re right, there couldn’t be an endless supply of those chickens. When you got close to graduation in high school, what kind of career, what were your prospects? What were you thinking of?

Well I was fortunate in that Freddie Hubbard and James Spaulding and a lot of us, we had our own little bands and we were playing jazz. In fact we had a hot little band. My uncle was friendly with some gentlemen who owned a club in Indianapolis. And we had a gig, we worked six nights a week with two matinees, and we were just teenagers. We were playing all the Art Blakey Jazz Messenger, Clifford Brown, Max Roach charts and everything. And we had a piano player by the name of Al Plank, a white guy who lives in San Francisco now, been living there for several years, and he was — he was not out first pianist, we had another guy Walt Miller who was the original pianist — but then Al Plank came in. And Al had the ability to help write a lot of arrangements and then Freddie and we all contributed some stuff to the repertoire. But we gained a reputation
throughout the midwest in terms of our little group. And I had my first road gig when I was sixteen, with Conte Candoli.
The Jazz Contemporaries, yeah. That was the group.
